decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach, rotating open gripper toward the mallet; right arm stays clear.
Approach the visible handle while finishing downward gripper orientation; leave clearance for visual alignment.
Lower and shift left/back to the handle, using flange-to-gripper offset rather than treating EE as fingertips.
Correct the visual approach forward/right; keep gripper open and retain elbow-up configuration.
Center the handle in the wrist view and lower toward grasp depth with small aligned movements.
Make a small lateral centering correction, then close around the handle. Retention will be checked by lifting.
Finish closing and lift the mallet vertically to check visual retention before moving over the keys.
Mallet is visibly retained. Move above the leftmost key and turn the shaft rightward, keeping the left hand in its workspace.
Strike the leftmost red key vertically, then lift 4 cm before any lateral move.
Advance to the orange key while raised, strike vertically, then lift over 2.5 cm; keep the mallet closed in the left gripper.
Continue left-to-right to the yellow key, descend for a strike, and lift 4.5 cm before advancing.
Strike the fourth, green key and lift 4.5 cm, maintaining the left-hand grasp and elbow-up posture.
Move to the fifth cyan key, strike and lift 4.5 cm. Keep the left flange on the left side of the workspace.
Strike the sixth blue key and lift clear. Keep the left flange left of center; remaining keys will use the mallet's reach.
Raise and swing the mallet toward the seventh purple key without moving the left hand across center.
Strike the seventh purple key and lift 4 cm, holding lateral position and mallet orientation.
Raise and swing the retained mallet toward the rightmost key while keeping the left hand left of center and the other arm clear.
Replan after continuity rejection: use much smaller increments and slightly lower the hover while aligning the final key.
Strike the eighth, rightmost magenta key, then lift the mallet 4.2 cm while retaining the grasp.
Lift farther after the final strike to ensure the mallet tip clears the key by more than 2.5 cm; retract slightly to keep configuration margin.
Return above the first key with ample clearance to repeat the sequence using larger tip lifts; earlier short lifts may not have cleared enough.
Replan the rejected return at half-sized increments, staying high above the keys.
Complete the elevated return above the first red key, retaining the mallet and elbow-up configuration.
Lower over the first key for a visually checked strike depth before lifting and repeating the ordered sequence.
Make a slow additional downward approach at the first red key to resolve uncertain tip contact, without lateral scraping.
Lift clear of the red key by 5.4 cm, advance to orange, and strike using the visually checked lower contact depth.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion: lift from orange, move to yellow, and strike; right arm remains stationary.
Lift over 5 cm from yellow before moving to and striking the fourth green key.
Lift from green, advance one key right to cyan, and strike vertically at the checked contact depth.
Lift clear of cyan, advance to the sixth blue key, and strike while keeping the left flange left of center.
Lift over 5 cm from blue, then swing the mallet above the seventh purple key without crossing the arms.
Strike the seventh purple key at the checked lower depth, briefly settle, then lift 4.4 cm before advancing.
Swing the raised mallet onto the eighth magenta key with the left hand still left of center; avoid the previous high-hover continuity limit.
Strike the rightmost magenta key, briefly settle at contact depth, then lift the mallet 4.5 cm.
Lift farther after the final strike and retract safely, keeping the mallet closed and clear of all keys.
Hold the retained mallet above the instrument after the ordered strikes and final lift; await the next observation.
Contact remains uncertain from RGB. Return above the left side with clearance to improve tip-first alignment for the ordered strikes.
Continue the elevated return to the first key, with a slightly more central strike line along the bars.
Pitch the mallet tip downward above the first key so the ball, rather than the gripper, reaches the key first.
Strike the first red key with the downward-angled mallet tip, briefly settle, then lift 4.4 cm before moving right.
Advance to orange while lifted, strike with the downward-pitched mallet, and lift 4.5 cm.
Move to the third yellow key, strike with the pitched mallet tip, and lift 4.5 cm before the next key.
Advance to the fourth green key while raised, strike tip-first, then lift 4.5 cm.
Continue to the fifth cyan key, strike tip-first, and lift 4.5 cm while holding the mallet closed.
Strike the sixth blue key with a small mallet swing, keeping the left flange left of center; lift 4.5 cm afterward.
Swing the raised mallet to the seventh purple key while keeping the left hand in its own workspace and preserving elbow-up continuity.
Strike the seventh purple key tip-first and lift 4.5 cm before moving to the last key.
Align the downward-pitched mallet with the rightmost magenta key using small continuous movements; keep the left flange left of center.
Replan without further forward reach: make a small tip alignment onto the last key, strike downward, lift over 2.5 cm, then retract.
